headlines.article_text: Stellantis sees $4.5 billion cash drain, continues with turnaround plan Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Stellantis saw a $4.5 billion cash drain in the third quarter while revenues and operating profit rose. Michael Wayland / CNBC European car giant Stellantis reported a 4 billion euro ($4.5 billion) cash shortfall in the third quarter as it ploughed ahead with its $70 billion turnaround strategy to restore profitability. Third-quarter revenues rose 1% to 37.6 billion euros from a year ago, the Chrysler and Jeep owner said on Wednesday, while adjusted operating income rose 184% to 256 million euros from 90 million euros a year earlier. The company also reported that negative industrial free cash flow improved to 4 billion euros, up from 4.3 billion the year prior. Stellantis shares were up 3.6% shortly after the European market opened, but have declined 62% since the beginning of the year. Stellantis stock since the beginning of the year. The announcement came as the transatlantic company continues to implement a 60 billion euro ($66.7 billion) turnaround strategy after years of sales declines, especially in North America. Stellantis reaffirmed that it expects positive industrial free cash flow in 2027 "During the quarter, we continued to make progress in the early execution of our FaSTLAne 2030 plan, launching new products, accelerating partnerships as planned, and delivering meaningful improvements in manufacturing and quality," Stellantis CEO Antonio Filosa said in the report. In May, Filosa laid out a five-year plan to achieve positive free cash flow by 2027. This includes investing 36 billion euros in its portfolio of automotive brands, with 60% of the cash to go towards its struggling North America sector. It also plans to introduce new vehicles, refresh models, and incorporate new technologies in its products. China competition European carmakers, including Stellantis, have been struggling in China as domestic brands like Xiaomi, BYD and Geely gain ground and intensify competition. Just this week, German luxury carmaker Porsche said it would reduce its exposure to China as car sales decline in the region. Meanwhile, Mercedes-Benz said its third-quarter car sales slumped due to a "challenging market environment," in the country. Performance was also boosted by strong inflows into its global wealth management business. With the integration of former rival Credit Suisse “firmly on track” for completion by year-end, CEO Sergio Ermotti said the Swiss banking giant remains committed to its global and regional footprint. In this article UBS Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT This photograph shows a sign of Swiss giant banking UBS at a branch in Zurich on March 4, 2026. Fabrice Coffrini | AFP | Getty Images UBS reported a pretax profit of almost $3.6 billion in the third quarter, up 27% year over year, largely in line with consensus forecasts. The Swiss banking and asset management giant saw strong net inflows into its global wealth management business. Net profit was $2.7 billion for the third quarter, in line with estimates. UBS shares are up by around a quarter this year The Zurich-headquartered lender's common equity tier (CET) 1 capital ratio — a measure of a bank's solvency — reached 14.7% during the period, up from 14.4% the previous quarter. Strong inflows into its global wealth management business supported performance, with net new assets reaching $55.1 billion by the end of the quarter. UBS recorded $12.5 billion in client commitments across its wealth management and asset management businesses. In its third-quarter earnings statement Wednesday, the bank said the integration of Credit Suisse is "firmly on track" to be completed by year-end, delivering a total of $13.7 billion in cumulative cost savings, above earlier expectations of $13.5 billion. UBS battles with Swiss government over risk tools UBS remains locked in an ongoing wrangle with the Swiss government over proposals for increased capital buffers, aimed at insulating taxpayers from any future banking crisis and contagion from the bank's foreign subsidiaries following the Credit Suisse debacle. The bank is seen as systemically important to the Swiss economy. The country's upper house of parliament voted last month to require UBS to hold 90% of Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital, or about $16 billion in extra shares, as collateral to support its foreign subsidiaries. The level currently stands at around 45%. UBS wants it to be no more than 50%. Speaking with CNBC's "Squawk Box Europe" Wednesday, Ermotti said the bank's clients expect it to be competitive. "90% would not, long-term, allow us to be a competitive player," Ermotti told CNBC's Carolin Roth. "I'm very concerned about this development." In an earlier statement, Ermotti said UBS' strong third-quarter performance underlines the benefits of its diversified global business model, adding that the lender remains "strategically committed to its diversified business model and its global and regional footprint." headlines.article_text: Meta and Google-backed Jio Platforms’ shares soar over 21% on trading debut Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Jio raised 302 billion rupees ($3.2 billion) in the country's largest-ever IPO. Global brokerage Nomura on Wednesday gave Jio Platforms a buy rating. Signage for Jio Platforms Ltd. ahead of the company's listing ceremony at the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in Mumbai, India, on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. Bloomberg | Bloomberg | Getty Images Jio Platforms' shares rose 21.5% on their trading debut Wednesday after a record initial public offering that was lapped up by retail as well as institutional investors. Jio's market capitalization was 12.5 trillion rupees ($131 billion), making it the second most valued company in India after its parent Reliance Industries, as per NSE data. This paves the way for its eventual inclusion in key benchmark indices. That inclusion will generate sufficient demand and protect the share price from any oversupply, Deven Choksey, founder and managing director at wealth management firm DRChoksey FinServ, told CNBC. He added that some of the investors who acquired a stake in Jio around 2021 may want to exit in around six months, by which time the stock will likely be included in the MSCI index and the Nifty 50 . India's largest telecom and digital services player had offered 270 million shares in the IPO priced at 1,119 rupees apiece, raising 302 billion rupees ($3.2 billion) in the country's largest-ever IPO. The public issue was subscribed more than 22 times, with institutional investors leading the demand, according to data from the BSE. The qualified institutional portion was subscribed 70.55 times, while retail investors subscribed 2.72 times. The IPO was fully subscribed within 95 minutes of its opening on Oct. 21, Akash Ambani, managing director of Jio Platforms and heir of the Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani, said ahead of the listing. Global brokerage Nomura on Wednesday gave Jio Platforms a buy rating, setting a target price of 1,340 rupees, implying an upside of 19.7% to its IPO price. The brokerage said in a report that Jio's capex cycle is largely over and there is expected to be a sharp improvement in the company's free cash flow. Shares were last trading at 1,360 rupees. Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani's flagship company, Reliance Industries , owns more than a 66% stake in Jio Platforms, followed by Meta Platforms ' affiliate Jaadhu Holdings that owns nearly 10% and Google International, which owns 7.7%, as per LSEG data. Leading global funds such as BlackRock, Capital Group and GIC participated in Jio's anchor book portion of the total fundraise, which is set aside for large institutional investors before the IPO opens for public bidding.
